paper.title: A Trial of Lopinavir–Ritonavir in Adults Hospitalized with Severe Covid-19
paper.shortTitle: A Trial of Lopinavir–Ritonavir in Adults Hospitalized with Sev

thesis: In hospitalized adult patients with severe Covid-19, no benefit was observed with lopinavir–ritonavir treatment beyond standard care.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What effect or association is supported in the studied human population?

nodes.title: Choose cohort and endpoint
nodes.body: We conducted a randomized, controlled, open-label trial involving hospitalized adult patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, which causes the respiratory illness Covid-19, and an oxygen saturation (Sao2) of 94% or less while they were breathing ambient air or a ratio of the partial pressure of oxygen (Pao2) to the fraction of inspired oxygen (Fio2) of less than 300 mm Hg.

nodes.title: Measure human outcomes
nodes.body: Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either lopinavir–ritonavir (400 mg and 100 mg, respectively) twice a day for 14 days, in addition to standard care, or standard care alone.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: Treatment with lopinavir–ritonavir was not associated with a difference from standard care in the time to clinical improvement (hazard ratio for clinical improvement, 1.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.72).

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: In hospitalized adult patients with severe Covid-19, no benefit was observed with lopinavir–ritonavir treatment beyond standard care.
